mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is an Apostille Convention party; otherwise consular legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of Viet Nam in the issuing state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives and authorized signatories against the State Bank of Vietnam's customer due diligence framework, the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Vietnamese domestic counter-terrorism and anti-money-laundering lists. PEP status and close associates must be specifically identified, risk-rated, and subject to enhanced due diligence; refresher screening is required at least annually and upon any material ownership or control event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal of Viet Nam (Cổng Thông Tin Quốc Gia Về Đăng Ký Doanh Nghiệp) at https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official enterprise name must be in Vietnamese script in accordance with Articles 37-40 of the Law on Enterprises 2020 and Decree 01/2021/NĐ-CP. The name may include numerals and symbols but must not be identical or confusingly similar to a previously registered name. If a foreign-language name is used in the company charter, it must be transliterated or translated appropriately; the Vietnamese name remains the statutory registered name and all official filings must use Vietnamese spelling and orthography.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Viet Nam, Vietnamese, or expressions implying state sovereignty
Communist Party, public security, military, armed forces
Bank, credit institution, securities, insurance, investment fund
Terms reserved for licensed financial or regulated professions
Any token identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise name in the same industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may correct and resubmit the name through the National Business Registration Portal at no additional charge. To contest the rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative complaint with the Director of the Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment within the statutory appeal period under Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13. If the complaint is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Chairman of the Provincial People's Committee or initiate administrative proceedings before the competent provincial Administrative Court. Name reservation extensions are not separately granted; a fresh application with a corrected name is the practical recourse.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the sole registered office for a foreign-invested LLC in Viet Nam. A physical address in Viet Nam must be stated in both the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate. Virtual-office arrangements may only supplement, not replace, a physically verifiable leased or serviced address, and the registered address must be capable of receiving official notices and being inspected by state authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-Low; estimated 10-15% annual unannounced inspection risk for a standard digital-content foreign-invested LLC, increasing to High Probability if the registered office is a co-working address, if administrative documents are found inconsistent, or if UBO/sanctions screening flags heightened risk indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises (Luật Doanh nghiệp) No. 59/2020/QH14, dated 17 June 2020, effective 1 January 2021, as amended and supplemented, in particular Articles 25, 26, 28, 35, 36, 47, 48, 49, 50, 67, 73, 74, and 75; Law on Investment (Luật Đầu tư) No. 61/2020/QH14, in particular Articles 13, 22, 23, 24, 36, 37, 38, 39 and 40; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on Enterprise Registration, in particular Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 32; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP detailing the Law on Investment, in particular Articles 15, 16, 17, 20, 21, 22 and 38; Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP on Fire Safety and Fire Fighting; Law on Environmental Protection No. 72/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Agency for Business Registration (ABR) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment, operating the National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) at dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; locally competent authority is the Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province or centrally governed city in which the registered office of the Limited Liability Company is situated. If the company is established inside an industrial park, export processing zone, economic zone, or high-tech park, the competent authority is the Management Board of that zone. For investment registration, the competent authority is the DPI or the relevant Zone Management Board acting under the Law on Investment 2020 and Decree 31/2021/ND-CP.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: For a foreign-invested limited liability company: (i) Application for Investment Registration Certificate (Form I-01) and the enclosed investment project proposal for issuance of the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC); and (ii) Application for Enterprise Registration (Form A-01) together with the company Charter (Điều lệ công ty), the List of Members (Form A-07), the written statement of the legal representative, and the capital contribution schedule, which collectively constitute the enterprise registration dossier leading to the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Viet Nam does not impose a general statutory minimum charter capital, nor any mandatory escrow or blocked-account rule, for a foreign-invested limited liability company engaged in a non-conditional digital web fiction subscription and interactive reading platform business. The charter capital is freely determined by the founding members and must be declared truthfully and fully in the company Charter. Under Article 47(4) and Article 75(1) of the Law on Enterprises 2020, each member must contribute the subscribed capital in full within 90 days from the date of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate, by transferring the monetary contribution into a corporate bank account opened in the name of the company with a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam, or by completing registration of ownership transfer for non-cash contributions. The company must issue a capital contribution certificate to each contributing member. If, exceptionally, the company later enters a licensed or conditional industry requiring a higher charter capital (e.g., banking, insurance, telecommunication, education), a statutory minimum paid-up capital threshold may apply, and a deposit or escrow may be required by sector-specific legislation, but such threshold does not apply to the present ISIC 9000 digital content platform activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING MEMBERS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ADOPTED IN WRITING IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS] - WHEREAS the founding members have agreed to incorporate a limited liability company under the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and to operate a serialized digital web fiction subscription and interactive reading application platform (ISIC 9000; NAICS 511130); NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The company Charter (Điều lệ công ty) submitted for registration is adopted in full, and the company name, legal form, principal business scope, charter capital, duration, and domicile as stated in the Charter are approved. 2. The charter capital of Vietnamese Dong [VND] [insert amount] is subscribed severally and jointly by the founding members according to the List of Members, and each member shall make full payment of its subscribed portion no later than 90 days from the date of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate by transfer to the company's corporate bank account in Viet Nam or by lawful in-kind contribution, and the company shall issue capital contribution certificates to every contributing member. 3. The registered office of the company is adopted as [full address of registered office], and the Chairman and the General Director are jointly authorized to execute the office lease, pay deposits and rentals, procure office fit-out, and register the office address with all competent authorities. 4. The following officers are duly appointed to hold office from the date of this Resolution: (a) [Name] as Chairman and Legal Representative of the company; (b) [Name] as General Director / Chief Executive Officer with day-to-day management and representation authority within the limits of the Charter; and (c) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer / Chief Accountant responsible for accounting, tax filing, treasury, and banking relationships. 5. The company's bank accounts at [name of bank, branch] shall be opened, with dual-signature authority of the Chairman (or Legal Representative) and the General Director (or CFO), and all paid-up capital subscriptions shall be transferred into such accounts within the statutory deadline. 6. The company seal shall be produced through an authorized seal-engraving establishment and its sample shall be notified to the enterprise registration authority in the prescribed form and time. 7. The officers are instructed to complete the payment of incorporation fees, publication of establishment information on the National Enterprise Information Portal, tax and electronic invoice registration, labor and social insurance registration, and all environmental, fire safety, and occupational safety clearances required for the registered office, and to enter into the Apple App Store, Apple In-App Purchase (IAP), and Google Play Billing agreements in the name of the company. 8. All actions taken by the founders and their authorized representatives in preparation of the incorporation, including the filing of the Investment Registration Certificate application and the Enterprise Registration application, are ratified in their entirety. 9. Certified true copies of this Resolution shall be submitted to banks, lessors, notary offices, tax authorities, and government agencies as evidence of corporate authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Registration Certificate for the 100% Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province or centrally governed city where the registered office will be located, or the Management Board of the industrial park/economic zone/high-tech park if the office is inside such zone; applications are filed electronically through the National Investment Information System (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đầu tư) or directly at the one-stop-shop division of the competent authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign founding member prepares and files Form I-01 (Investment Registration Certificate Application) together with a concise investment project proposal describing the subscription-based web novel and interactive reading platform, the projected charter capital, the foreign investor's identity/corporate legal standing, and the proposed address of the registered office in Viet Nam. The application must confirm that the business scope is not on the list of prohibited or conditional sectors, or, if conditional, must annex the sector-specific pre-approval. The competent DPI or Zone Management Board reviews the dossier for form and substance, consults relevant ministries only if a sectoral condition is triggered, and issues the IRC carrying the project code and investment incentives (if any). The IRC is a prerequisite to enterprise registration for a foreign-invested company.
required_dossiers: Application for Investment Registration Certificate (Form I-01)
Investment project proposal or feasibility statement covering the market, content moderation process, technology platform, financials, and proposed scale of operations
Draft company Charter (Điều lệ công ty) for the limited liability company to be established

Certified legal identity document of the foreign investor (passport for natural persons or certificate of incorporation/legal existence for corporate investors, consular legalized and Vietnamese-translated where required)
Power of attorney to the domestic law firm or authorized local contact (if signed outside Viet Nam, legalized)
Proposed registered office lease agreement, memorandum of lease, or letter of intent from the lessor (if already available)
Audited financial statements or solvency evidence of the foreign investor, if required by the competent authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is incomplete or deficient, the competent authority issues a written request for supplementation within 5 working days; the applicant may cure the deficiencies within 30 working days without refiling from scratch. If the IRC application is rejected, the applicant may amend and resubmit the dossier, request reconsideration with the DPI Director, or appeal to the Ministry of Planning and Investment and subsequently to the provincial People's Court pursuant to the Law on Handling of Administrative Violations and Decree 31/2021/ND-CP.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization, and Consular Legalization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vietnamese notary offices (Văn phòng công chứng) for signature attestation; provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) for the eventual acceptance of the enterprise registration dossier; Foreign Affairs offices or Vietnamese consular missions for legalization of foreign documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal counsel drafts the company Charter, List of Members, capital contribution schedule, and the written Statement on Establishment in Vietnamese. Each founding member and the proposed legal representative sign the charter. Foreign documents not executed in Viet Nam must be consular legalized and translated into Vietnamese with certified translation; documents executed in Viet Nam are notarized at a licensed notary office. The digital signature infrastructure (V-SDC or USB token) of the legal representative is prepared for the electronic filing on the National Business Registration Portal.
required_dossiers: Draft company Charter in Vietnamese signed by all founding members
List of Members and capital contribution schedule (Form A-07)
Written statement of the legal representative undertaking lawful management and truthful submission
Passport or identity card copies of all founding members, the Chairman, the General Director, and the Legal Representative (with notarization or legalization)
Power of attorney for signatories outside Viet Nam
Certified translation of foreign corporate registration documents or passports where required
Draft registered office lease contract and certificate of the property owner if the lease is not in the company's ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify due to defective signatures, the affected page is re-signed in the notary's presence and re-attested; if consular legalization is queried, the document must be authenticated by the issuing jurisdiction's competent ministry and re-submitted to the Vietnamese consulate. Administrative delays of the notary do not prejudice the applicant beyond the published fee schedule; the applicant may select another notary office. If certified translations contain errors, a corrected translation is filed before the DPI review deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Check and Electronic Filing of the Enterprise Registration Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration System (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) operated by the Agency for Business Registration (ABR) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment; final legal review by the provincial Department of Planning and Investment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before submitting, the applicant performs an online name search to verify that the proposed Vietnamese name of the company is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name in compliance with Articles 37, 38, 39 and 41 of the Law on Enterprises 2020. The applicant then completes electronic Form A-01, annexes the Charter and List of Members, attaches the valid Investment Registration Certificate, and submits the dossier with the digital signature of the legal representative (or authorized person) via the National Business Registration Portal. The system validates the dossier and assigns a reference number. The submission replaces physical submission; the applicant may monitor status electronically.
required_dossiers: Form A-01 - Application for Enterprise Registration
Approved company Charter signed by all founding members
Form A-07 - List of Members with subscribed and paid capital ratios
Written consent to act of the Legal Representative, Chairman, General Director, and Chief Accountant
Valid Investment Registration Certificate (for foreign-invested LLC)
Certified legalized passports or corporate registration documents of foreign members
Consular legalized / notarized power of attorney of the authorized filer (if any)
Digital signature token (V-SDC / USB token) of the Legal Representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the system identifies a name collision or confusing similarity, the applicant must select a new name and resubmit, without additional state fee, provided the initial submission was not formally registered. If the application is returned due to invalid digital signature or unsupported document format, the applicant corrects the format and re-submits within the same day. If the DPI issues an incompleteness notification within 3 working days, the applicant has 30 days to supplement through the portal; failure to cure results in automatic termination of the application, upon which a fresh application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Enterprise Registration Certificate and Automatic Tax Identification Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) issuing the Enterprise Registration Certificate through the National Business Registration System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The DPI examines the electronic dossier. If the dossier is valid, the DPI issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) within 3 working days after receipt of the valid application and payment of the state fee. The ERC is accompanied by the enterprise code and enterprise tax identification number (Mã số thuế), which are legally identical. The ERC will state the company's registration number, legal form, charter capital, registered office, legal representative, and principal business activities (including ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130 digital web fiction and interactive reading application). Upon issuance, the company acquires full legal personality, but certain operational permits remain to be obtained before entry into operation (e.g., fire safety and invoice registration, if applicable).
required_dossiers: Deposit slip or online payment confirmation of the enterprise registration state fee (VND 100,000) and, where applicable, the IRC issuance fee (VND 1,000,000)
Reference number of the accepted electronic dossier on dak, external
No additional dossier is required if the electronic submission was complete; original paper documents need not be submitted unless the DPI so requests
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the 3-working-day deadline lapses without action, the applicant may lodge a written complaint with the Director of the DPI or the provincial People's Committee, and may demand the certificate ex officio in accordance with Article 26(4) of the Law on Enterprises 2020. If the ERC contains an error in the enterprise code, capital, legal representative, or registered address, the company files a corrected enterprise registration (Form A-00) with the DPI to replace the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporation Seal Creation and Seal Sample Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) for receipt of the seal sample notification; the seal is physically manufactured by a licensed seal-engraving establishment (Cơ sở khắc dấu) authorized under Decree 01/2021/ND-CP.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the ERC, the Legal Representative selects an authorized seal-engraving service and gives the engraver the lawfully issued ERC. The seal must contain the exact enterprise name and enterprise code. The company then submits a Notice of Seal Sample (Form A-12) through the National Business Registration Portal within 30 days from the date of ERC issuance. The seal may be used immediately upon creation, but must be kept under the custody and control of the Legal Representative or an officer delegated by the Legal Representative. The DPI issues a seal sample receipt; subsequent seal changes or destruction are again notified to the DPI.
required_dossiers: Form A-12 - Notice of Seal Sample (with the exact image of the seal affixed/uploaded)
Copy of the Enterprise Registration Certificate
Identity document of the Legal Representative
Copy of the seal-engraving establishment's authorization, if requested by the DPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal sample notification is deficient because the seal text does not match the ERC, the company re-engraves the seal at a licensed establishment and re-notifies the corrected sample. If the DPI queries the authenticity of the seal-engraver, the company annexes the seal-engraving establishment's business registration certificate. Failure to notify the seal sample is subject to administrative fine under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; the remedy is immediate late notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Establishment Information on the National Enterprise Information Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agency for Business Registration (ABR) through the National Enterprise Information Portal (Trang thông tin doanh nghiệp), Ministry of Planning and Investment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of the Enterprise Registration Certificate issuance, the DPI transmits the company's core registration particulars to the National Enterprise Information Portal for public posting. The company verifies the published content: enterprise name, code, head office, legal representative, charter capital, members, and line of business. The company pays the publication fee (approximately VND 300,000) online through the portal, which completes the statutory publication requirement. The publication does not require a separate paper filing.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate reference number
No separate application document; publication is automatically linked to the registration record
Proof of payment of the publication fee (online receipt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal records are inaccurately transcribed, the company submits a correction request to the DPI with evidence of the ERC. If publication is omitted due to non-payment, the company pays the fee and the publication is back-dated; continuing omission is sanctioned by Decree 122/2021/ND-CP, and the penalty is paid without prejudice to the legal validity of the ERC.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) of the Ministry of Finance of Viet Nam; National e-Tax portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn) and National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested LLC obtains its Enterprise Registration Certificate through the National Business Registration Portal; the tax registration and issuance of the Tax Identification Number (Mã số thuế, MST) occur automatically through the administrative single-window mechanism. The LLC must additionally complete a VAT registration dossier with the competent local tax sub-department within 15 days of the Enterprise Registration Certificate date and register for the e-invoice system under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP. The MST serves as both the corporate income tax account number and the VAT identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a foreign-invested LLC is a resident enterprise taxable at the corporate level; no pass-through election is available. Territorial_Scope — resident enterprises are taxed on worldwide income, with double-tax relief for foreign-source income under applicable tax treaties and domestic unilateral credit rules. No Tax_Exempt_Zone applies to the ordinary LLC; only Export Processing Enterprises (EPE) located in recognized export processing zones or industrial zones would benefit from special fiscal zone treatment, which is not assumed here.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam has no check-the-box entity classification election analogous to the U.S. regime. Available elections include: (i) voluntary VAT registration under the credit (input-deduction) method instead of the direct method, which is mandatory once annual turnover exceeds VND 1 billion; (ii) election to file consolidated withholding-tax settlements for related-party cross-border transactions; (iii) election to apply a simplified VAT declaration for micro entities where statutorily eligible; and (iv) application of the Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) regime only for non-resident contractors, not for the domestic LLC. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Decree 132/2020/ND-CP adopts hybrid-mismatch anti-avoidance rules without elective features.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Thuế Giá trị Gia tăng, GTGT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applies to a resident LLC: VAT registration is mandatory from the date of enterprise registration irrespective of revenue. For non-resident digital suppliers with no place of business in Viet Nam, the threshold is VND 100,000,000 per calendar year under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC; this foreign-supplier threshold is inapplicable to the resident VN_LLC but establishes the domestic nexus baseline for cross-border platform payment flows.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing applies under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. From 1 July 2022, all taxpayers must issue e-invoices with a certified digital signature of the e-invoice service provider and transmit invoice data to the General Department of Taxation via the National e-Tax portal. Retail sales to consumers effected through the app must be documented by cash-register e-invoices (hóa đơn điện tử khởi tạo từ máy tính tiền) transmitted in near real time to the tax authority. The issuer must adopt an API-integrated clearance or periodic XML upload satisfying the GDT data format, and e-invoices must carry the national fiscal serial number and QR code issued by licensed Viet Nam e-invoice service providers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods and services are subject to 0% VAT under Article 9 of Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC. A resident LLC may apply 0% VAT to web-novel subscription and interactive reading services only where the services are supplied under a written contractual agreement to a foreign customer (non-resident), are consumed wholly outside Viet Nam, and are settled in foreign currency through a licensed Vietnamese bank. Services rendered to foreign principals but consumed in Viet Nam, and services evidenced by domestic top-up or App-Store settlement flows, remain standard-rated at 10%. Consequently, Apple IAP and Google Play Billing flows require re-invoicing to the offshore platform operator together with a contract and offshore-consumption evidence to sustain 0% treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (not applicable to pure digital services; replaced by a duly executed Service Export Contract identifying the offshore recipient and containing an offshore-consumption clause)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (not required for digital services; substituted by the web-novel platform's delivery and usage logs evidencing offshore subscriber consumption)
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds through a licensed Vietnamese bank within the statutory repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unfounded zero-rating claims are scrutinized by GDT audits using transfer-pricing and offshore-consumption tests. Consequences include: retrospective clawback of input VAT credits; imposition of 10% VAT (or 20% where fraudulent misclassification is established) on the full gross consideration; late-payment interest of 0.03% per day on the underdeclared tax under Article 59 of the Law on Tax Administration; administrative fines up to VND 500,000,000 under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; and criminal sanctions for tax evasion under Article 200 of the Penal Code, including fines up to VND 4,500,000,000 or imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years, with additional prohibition on tax-refund claims and denial of input VAT offsets for up to 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) – Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam, together with the Foreign Exchange Control Ordinance and Circular No. 15/2015/TT-NHNN (and successor amendments) guiding foreign exchange activities, including current account and capital account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vietnamese đồng (VND) is not fully freely convertible. Current account transactions, including remittances for trade in services and software/content licensing, are generally permitted and may be freely effected through authorized credit institutions, subject to underlying documentation and MT103/RCD purpose codes. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections for a foreign-invested LLC and outbound remittances of dividends or liquidation proceeds after annual audit and tax clearance, require registration with the SBV (e.g., Foreign Investment Registration Certificate / Investment Registration Certificate, registration of capital account via the enterprise's direct investment capital account (DICA) at a licensed bank). Profit remittance hurdles: annual financial statements must be audited, all corporate income tax and VAT obligations settled, and the remittance supported by audited statement, tax finalization proof, and a legalized corporate resolution. Capital contribution must be fully paid within the timeframe and registered with the SBV via the DICA. Foreign loan disbursements require SBV registration under Circular 12/2022/TT-NHNN for medium to long-term foreign loans. No general capital controls beyond transaction-level documentary compliance; dividends on foreign investment may be repatriated annually after satisfying all financial obligations and tax certifications.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vietnam has substantially liberalized surrender requirements. As of recent regimes, exporters are not broadly mandated to surrender 100% of export proceeds to the SBV; however, authorized dealers must receive export earnings into a foreign currency account domiciled in Vietnam within the statutory period (generally not exceeding 180 days from customs clearance, unless extended under Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN or successor regulations). Mandatory conversion exists only for certain state-enterprise or special categories; for a private LLC, the requirement is to repatriate and deposit export receipts into a licensed bank's foreign currency account, convert to VND as needed for operational/tax obligations. The statutory timeline for reporting and supporting documentation includes submitting the B2 declaration and underlying invoices through the bank's electronic system, with a general 180-day collection horizon for services/digital exports unless a SBV/Treasury-approved longer term is obtained.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietcombank (Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account + Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BIDV (Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam)
VietinBank (Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium -- Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Aspire) are not licensed banks in Vietnam and cannot provide local VND settlement, DICA custody, or SBV compliance services. They may be used only as auxiliary receivable collection tools for low-risk digital subscription receipts in foreign currency, provided funds are swept promptly into a licensed Vietnamese bank account and transferwise-style peer-to-peer settlement does not violate Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN. The digital platform's direct debit from Apple/Google via IAP and Play Billing generally settles in USD or local App Store currencies into the EMI, but Vietnamese foreign exchange control requires the operating company to repatriate export earnings to a licensed bank in Vietnam and document the cross-border service sale. Full reliance on EMIs is legally non-viable as the primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is practically mandatory for a newly incorporated foreign-invested LLC in Vietnam. Bank compliance officers require the legal representative and, for foreign shareholders, the overseas corporate director/shareholder's authorized signatories to appear at the bank's head office or designated transaction office for identity verification and signing of account opening documentation. Remote opening is not generally permitted; some banks allow pre-screening online but final wet-ink signatures and in-person interviews at the Vietnam branch are required. Foreign directors who are not tax-resident in Vietnam may be required to execute a power of attorney to a Vietnam-resident legal representative, with notarization and legalization by Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate, followed by physical appearance of the authorized person at the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) resides in a high-risk jurisdiction or appears in sanctions lists; offshore parent holding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of Articles of Association/Memorandum of Association of each layer up to ultimate shareholders; passport copies with notarization; corporate registry extracts (Business Registration Certificate / Investment Registration Certificate) apostilled or consular-legalized; source of funds evidence including board minutes, subscription agreements, bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital cross-border revenue model (web novel subscriptions through Apple IAP / Google Play) flagged as intangible/software royalty with transfer pricing or foreign currency concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service description and technical documentation distinguishing distinct original literary content creation and platform access from pure software license; content delivery architecture; ISIC 9000 classification certificate; transfer pricing policy documentation (Form 03/TK) and intercompany agreements between content platform, payment processors, and the VN LLC; historical revenue reports from Apple/Google seller portals showing gross billings, commissions, and net remittances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign capital contribution routed through founder personal account instead of direct corporate DICA.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DICA opening confirmation from licensed Vietnamese bank; corporate capital contribution identification number (Mã số định danh khoản góp vốn) issued by the bank; Share Register; Investment Registration Certificate showing requested capital and ownership ratio; SBV capital contribution registration confirmation; source-of-funds statement from each shareholder's parent bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity of subscription receipts in multiple foreign currencies (USD, EUR, JPY) without corresponding contract documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription terms of service, Apple Developer Program agreement, Google Play Distribution Agreement, merchant service agreements with ADC/Google Ireland/Google Asia Pacific; month-end reconciliation statements; tax invoices/e-invoices under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP; transfer pricing and CbC documentation if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential nexus for a deemed permanent establishment due to remote administration by offshore parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vietnam management location documentation: employment contracts and payroll records for Vietnam-resident GM and finance staff; physical office lease; board meeting minutes evidencing substantive decision-making in Vietnam; substance calendars, corporate insurance policies, and utility records in Vietnam.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the VN LLC's Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA / Tài khoản vốn đầu tư trực tiếp) maintained at a licensed Vietnamese commercial bank. The wire should specify purpose code consistent with SBV reporting, e.g., 'Góp vốn đầu tư nước ngoài – Foreign Direct Investment Capital Contribution' and reference the Investment Registration Certificate number and Enterprise Registration Code. The bank will validate the capital contribution against the DICA registration and issue an inward capital contribution confirmation code under Circular 06/2019/TT-NHNN as amended by Circular 03/2021/TT-NHNN. Loan disbursements from foreign shareholders or third-party lenders above 36 months must be registered with SBV under Circular 12/2022/TT-NHNN before drawdown; the loan proceeds must be credited to the DICA or a separate foreign loan account. No conversion into VND beyond ordinary working capital needs is permitted without underlying transaction documentation. The company must report changes to registered capital and foreign ownership to the SBV and the Department of Planning and Investment within prescribed timelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and operational outflows (content licensing fees, translation services, advertising, AWS hosting, sub-contractors), use SWIFT MT103/MT202 via the VN LLC's operational VND or foreign currency account at a licensed bank, with accurate remittance purpose codes per SBV current account classification. For commercial transactions involving cross-border goods (e.g., merchandise tie-ins), use documentary collection or Letter of Credit (MT700/MT707) through an advised/confirming bank; however, for digital services and intangibles, telegraphic transfer against invoices is standard. Payments for imports of services and royalties require supporting service contracts, VAT/e-invoices, tax withholding certificates, and transfer pricing documentation. All outbound remittances above reporting thresholds or those with consistency concerns may require bank-level compliance review; SBV reporting must be made through the bank's electronic systems. For dividend distributions, use MT103 after obtaining audited financial statements, CIT finalization, and a board resolution declaring the dividend; remit from the after-tax retained earnings account to the foreign shareholder's account using the purpose code 'Dividend remittance (Chuyển lợi nhuận ra nước ngoài)' and submit capital transfer reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (USD/VND and USD/foreign currency) with licensed Vietnamese banks on the basis of genuine trade or service transaction, permitted under SBV Forward Contract regulations (Circular 02/2003/TT-NHNN and successor Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN); no speculative positions permitted.

FX swaps (cross-currency swaps between VND and foreign currencies) with authorized credit institutions for cash-flow hedging of operational receipts and payables, limited to transactions with underlying real exposure.

NDFs (Non-Deliverable Forwards) are not legally tradable onshore for VND against USD; only deliverable forwards, swaps, and options (options with exception for certain permitted underlying) are permissible onshore. Offshore NDF markets for VND are prohibited for Vietnamese residents; hedging must be done onshore with a licensed bank.

Currency options (foreign currency options) to hedge known foreign currency cash flows, permitted with authorized dealers where underlying commercial transactions exist; premium payments and settlement in VND or foreign currency as per SBV authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (VAS) submitted to the tax authority and the provincial Department of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation via e-tax portal; provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI); National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (calendar year ending 31 December; filing deadline 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to VND 100,000,000 (approx USD 4,000) for late or non-lodged financial statements; late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on any tax underpayment; repeated non-compliance may lead to forced dissolution under Article 207 of the Law on Enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) finalization return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Sub-Department under the General Department of Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the third month following fiscal year-end (31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; administrative fine of 10%–20% of under-declared CIT for misstatement and up to VND 100,000,000 for failure to file, under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business license fee (Lệ phí môn bài) renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 January of each calendar year; for a newly formed enterprise, within 30 days of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the unpaid fee; administrative fine up to VND 10,000,000; tax authority debt-collection measures may be applied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Public disclosure of annual financial statements on the National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Business Registration Portal (NBRP) administered by the Ministry of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 days of financial statement approval and no later than 100 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to VND 20,000,000 for non-publication; the DPI may issue a binding publication order; unresolved publication failure may obstruct new investment procedures or enterprise registration amendments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all foreign-invested enterprises (FIEs) in Vietnam, including this LLC, regardless of turnover, total assets, or employee headcount; the requirement arises from the Law on Independent Audit and Decree 17/2021/ND-CP.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) as prescribed by the Law on Accounting 2015 and Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; IFRS permitted only for consolidated financial statements of designated enterprises following the Ministry of Finance IFRS roadmap.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam does not currently operate a separate annual UBO confirmation return filed with the corporate registry. However, the LLC must maintain complete and current beneficial ownership records under Decree 02/2019/ND-CP as amended by Decree 53/2023/ND-CP and the Law on Anti-Money Laundering 2022; UBO details must be re-verified within 10 calendar days of any member or shareholding transfer, and a risk-based customer due diligence refresh at least annually is the accepted standard. Any membership change also must be reported to the provincial DPI within 10 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (capital contribution and ownership percentage ledger)
Register of Directors (management appointments, Members' Council resolutions, and resignations)
Minute Book (shareholders' meetings, members' meetings, board resolutions, and consent minutes)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT rate is 20%. Preferential rates available under Law on Corporate Income Tax No. 14/2008/QH12 (as amended) include: (i) 10% for 15 years for qualifying high-tech, large-scale manufacturing, and new investment projects in eligible sectors or locations; (ii) 15% for new investment projects in certain difficult socio-economic areas; (iii) CIT exemption for 4 years and 50% reduction for the next 9 years for qualifying new investment projects in extremely difficult socio-economic areas or high-tech zones; (iv) 10% rate applicable to income from agricultural extension, agricultural breeding/processing in difficult areas, and socialized education/healthcare sectors. Small and micro enterprises may benefit from reduced rates: 15% for annual taxable income up to VND 3 billion, and 17% for annual taxable income up to VND 50 billion (valid through the relevant extended period under Resolution and CIT law amendments). Incentive eligibility requires an approved investment certificate (IRC/ERC) and satisfaction of the relevant conditionality. The taxpayer must apply incentives on the CIT finalization return and maintain separate accounting for incentivized and non-incentivized income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CIT Finalization Return Form 03/TNDN (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN) prescribed under Circular No. 151/2014/TT-BTC, as amended by Circular No. 96/2015/TT-BTC and Circular No. 80/2021/TT-BTC; electronic filing via the General Department of Taxation National e-Tax Portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn) using the e-Tax software (HTKK - Hỗ trợ kê khai).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT finalization return must be filed no later than the 90th day from the end of the fiscal year. If the fiscal year coincides with the calendar year, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. Quarterly provisional CIT declarations (Form 01/TNDN) are due by the 30th day of the first month of the following quarter, and provisional CIT payments for each quarter must be made by the 30th day of the first month of the next quarter. The finalization return itself is due by day 90 after fiscal year-end. If the deadline falls on a public holiday or weekend, the deadline is extended to the next working day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (MST), enterprise name, address, tax authority code, fiscal year, form of investment certificate, accounting regime, and industry code; must match the e-registration records in the national business registration database.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-invested LLC registered in Vietnam is a resident enterprise; enter the local tax code issued by the provincial tax department. Non-resident investors do not file this form themselves; the local entity is the withholding agent for distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue and other income attributable to the fiscal year, including sales of webnovel subscription services, virtual coin tokens, reading packages, advertisement income, and other operating income; revenue recognition per Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC and VAS 14.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign-owned LLC recognizes revenue in its Vietnamese statutory books on an accrual basis. Cross-border income derived through app stores must be recorded gross or net of platform commissions strictly in accordance with Circular 200 and tax rulings on Netting arrangements; do not net Apple/Google commissions for CIT purposes unless a substantive agency analysis supports gross reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable expenses incurred for the production of taxable income, including editorial costs, hosting fees, payment processing fees, marketing expenses, royalties, staff costs, depreciation, and other expenses satisfying the actual, reasonable, and adequately invoiced requirements of Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC (Article 4).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses with valid Vietnamese invoices, foreign invoices certified by the competent foreign authority and lawfully used, or customs vouchers are deductible. Intercompany fees must satisfy arm's length standards and be supported by a transfer pricing documentation file to avoid disallowance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses available for offset against current-year taxable income; losses may be carried forward 5 consecutive years from the year immediately after the loss year; carryback is not permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC as a resident taxpaying entity utilizes the loss carryforward; foreign shareholders cannot directly offset Vietnamese entity losses against their home-country income absent applicable foreign tax credit rules outside this filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D - Income entitled to CIT incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate schedule and calculation for income eligible for tax holidays, preferential rates, or 50% reduction; requires an investment certificate and satisfaction of incentive conditions; incentivized and non-incentivized income must be segregated with allocation keys clearly explained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign-owned LLC operates a digital serialization platform without a statutory investment license in a high-tech zone, it generally will not qualify for tax holidays; do not over-claim incentives absent an explicit IRC approval covering the activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Comparison of total provisional quarterly CIT paid against final annual liability; any shortfall is payable before the finalization deadline; penalties at 0.03% per day on late payment apply, and late payment interest may apply at 0.03% per day under the Tax Administration Law 38/2019/QH14.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-invested LLC must self-adjust and pay the difference no later than March 31 (calendar-year basis). If the final liability exceeds provisional payments by more than 20%, certain administrative scrutiny applies; ensure quarterly provisional accruals are reasonably aligned.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT finalization return attracts a penalty of VND 5,000,000 for returns filed 01-30 days late; VND 8,000,000 for 31-60 days late; VND 15,000,000 for 61-90 days late; and VND 30,000,000 for more than 90 days late, before any underpayment sanction. Underpayment of tax is subject to a late payment interest charge of 0.03% per day on the outstanding amount for each day of delay. Tax evasion or fraudulent understatement of revenue may be penalized at 20% or 100% of the under-declared tax amount depending on the nature of the violation, plus administrative fines and potential criminal liability under Article 200 Penal Code 2015 for tax evasion amounts of VND 100,000,000 or more. Failure to submit transfer pricing documentation, if selected for TP inspection, may result in a penalty of 50% of the TP adjustment amount plus late interest, and penalties for failing to submit prescribed TP forms and locational savings information.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: In general, dividends paid by a Vietnamese limited liability company to its foreign corporate shareholders are subject to Corporate Income Tax at the rate of 10% of the dividend distribution amount, unless the foreign shareholder qualifies for a treaty rate reduction under an applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA). While Vietnam does not impose a separate final dividend withholding tax under the Law on CIT, the 10% is effectively collected as CIT on dividend income of the foreign corporate recipient. Dividends distributed to foreign individuals are subject to a final personal income tax rate of 5% (not applicable to intercompany repatriation).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief (typically reducing the Vietnamese dividend tax to 5% or 0% depending on ownership thresholds and treaty terms), the foreign corporate shareholder must: (i) be the beneficial owner of the dividend; (ii) hold the requisite ownership percentage (usually at least 10% of charter capital and paid-up capital for the 5% rate, or 25% for a 0% rate under treaties such as the Vietnam-Singapore or Vietnam-Hong Kong DTA, subject to conditions); (iii) obtain and submit a valid Residency Certificate (Certificate of Tax Residence - TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction; (iv) complete the Tax Registration for Withholding at Reduced Rate process under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC and submit form FT002 or the applicable reduced-withholding form to the Vietnamese tax administration, either before or at the time the dividend is declared, as designated by the local tax authority; (v) provide legal documentation, namely business registration, certificate of incorporation, confirmation of beneficial ownership, and an affidavit that the shareholder does not have a permanent establishment in Vietnam to which the dividends are effectively connected; and (vi) respond to any additional request from the Vietnam tax authority for substance and anti-treaty-shopping information within the statutory time limit. The provincial tax department may issue a written confirmation of reduced withholding eligibility, and the local LLC is obliged to implement the reduced rate only after receipt of the approval or within the standard deadline under applicable DTA procedure. Failure to file the treaty relief procedure in advance may result in the full 10% being collected and the foreign shareholder having to subsequently claim a refund (and the local payer is at risk of being treated as having satisfied its withholding obligation only at the statutory rate).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For cross-border royalties, the statutory Combination CIT plus Foreign Contractor Withholding Tax (FCWT) rate is 10% CIT + 5% VAT on the deemed value for royalty payments to a foreign non-resident under Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC, being an aggregate effective statutory burden of 15% on gross royalty payments, unless a DTA reduces the royalty CIT rate to 7.5% or 10% (or other treaty-specific percentage). For interest, the statutory FCWT combination is 5% CIT (with no VAT) on gross cross-border interest, unless the applicable DTA reduces the interest withholding tax to 10% or 5% (depending on treaty). The DOI (Double Taxation Agreement) rate and reduced WHT procedure require the same TRC and beneficial ownership procedure as described for dividends. Where an intra-group financing or royalty payment is concluded not to be arm's length, the Vietnamese tax authority may disregard or recharacterize the payment; the payer is then denied a deduction and may be subject to deemed distributions treated as dividends subject to the dividend CIT rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Vietnam's Decree 132/2020/ND-CP requires the preparation and maintenance of transfer pricing documentation (TP file), including the Master File, Local File, and Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) thresholds. The Local File is mandatory for a taxpayer that is a related-party transaction participant and satisfies at least one of the following thresholds: (i) total related-party turnover for the period exceeding VND 50 billion (approximately US$2.1 million); or (ii) total related-party transactions in the tax year exceeding VND 30 billion (approximately US$1.3 million); or (iii) the taxpayer is a party to any transaction qualifying for the profit-based method and has applied the DTA benefit. The Master File must be prepared where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent exceeds VND 50 trillion (VND 50,000 billion, approximately US$2.1 billion) and any Vietnamese entity is the ultimate parent or is required to file CbCR. The CbCR is required where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent exceeds VND 18,000 billion (approximately US$775 million) and the group operates in more than one country. However, even where thresholds are not met, the taxpayer must still maintain sufficient documentation to demonstrate arm's length pricing, and the General Department of Taxation may request contemporaneous documentation in a TP audit. Starting with assessment periods from 2025 tax year onwards (under Decree 132 as amended and official guidance), certain high-risk taxpayers or taxpayers above the safe-harbor thresholds, including those carrying out digital business activities with related parties, may be placed into mandatory TP documentation requirements. A safe-harbor exists for taxpayers with low related-party turnover and limited related-party transactions (under VND 10 billion turnover and normal profit margins) allowing exemption from preparing the formal TP file, but the exemption is not a bar to adjustment if the return is materially incorrect.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not have a formal standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime equivalent to the UAE ESR. However, the following doctrines impose economic substance and anti-avoidance requirements: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under the Law on Tax Administration 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, which empowers the tax authority to re-determine tax obligations where a transaction is not economically substantive and is conducted mainly to avoid CIT; (ii) the beneficial ownership requirement embedded in each applicable DTA and Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC's anti-treaty-abuse provisions; and (iii) the substance-over-form principle embedded in the application of Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC for foreign contractor tax, and in the transfer pricing rules under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP regarding related-party transactions lacking commercial substance. In practice, a webnovel serial platform LLC with only a narrow profit margin, low payroll, and substantial remuneration paid abroad to a related marketing or licensing company may be challenged as lacking economic substance; the tax authority may apply the GAAR to ignore the transaction or re-characterize the arrangement, impose VAT and CIT on deemed revenue, and impose late payment interest and penalties. The protective response is to maintain real substantive operations in Vietnam: a physical production office in an industrial park or licensed digital content company, payroll and social insurance contributions, board meetings held in Vietnam, local service agreements and staff performing content curation, actual payment of Vietnamese suppliers, and a documented commercial rationale for all trademark, content-library, and marketing-related-party service arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Under-Declaration of Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately recording only a portion of the app-store and subscription revenue (e.g., under-recognizing Apple IAP and Google Play Billing receipts, using personal payment accounts, booking revenue net of commissions on an unapproved basis, or hiding overseas PayPal/Stripe collections), falsifying accounting ledgers, issuing or using illegal invoices, or structuring app-store payments to a related party to conceal taxable revenue in Vietnam.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative taxation penalties: additional tax assessment, payment of late payment interest at 0.03% per day, and penalties ranging from 20% to 100% of the under-declared tax amount. Criminal exposure under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015 (amended 2017): fine of VND 100,000,000 to VND 4,500,000,000 or imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years for tax evasion of between VND 100,000,000 and VND 4,500,000,000, with the upper thresholds rising to imprisonment of up to 20 years for amounts exceeding VND 4,500,000,000 in severe cases. The corporate entity is also subject to a fine of up to VND 3,000,000,000 and prohibition of business activities for a fixed period, depending on the aggregated amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives of the LLC are personally liable for tax offenses where the crime is committed on their orders or with their consent. The individual penal sanction can include imprisonment of up to 7 years for tax evasion plus monetary fines. Administrative restitution obligations attach to the legal representative; the director may be subject to a travel ban, exit suspension (cannot depart Vietnam until the tax debt and penalty are resolved), seizure of personal assets and bank accounts, and in cases of corporate veil piercing proof (fraudulent intent, abuse of limited liability, gross undercapitalization), the personal assets of shareholders and directors can be attached to satisfy tax liabilities. Where the evasion is proven to be organized at the director level, the director can face a criminal conviction, imprisonment, and a separate personal fine; additionally, the court may order the director to pay civil restitution to the state treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Substance Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Vietnamese LLC with no real editorial, sales, or operations substance; contracting-out all core functions to a related foreign entity; centralizing intangible ownership and content curation abroad solely to strip profit; claiming charges for marketing, licensing, or management services without commensurate value; arranging board decisions outside Vietnam to create the appearance of foreign management; maintaining a nominal local workforce with no authority to conduct business and no real control over the webnovel subscription platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, the tax authority will apply an arm's length re-determination: recharacterize the transactions, disallow the related-party deductions, impute profit to the Vietnamese LLC, and impose the resulting CIT (at 20% or preferential rate if applicable) plus late payment interest at 0.03% per day and a 20% or 40% administrative fine for mis-declaration. The foreign entity may simultaneously be subject to Foreign Contractor Tax (CIT + VAT) on its entire deemed Vietnamese-source income under Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC, creating a double economic burden. Where the arrangement is assessed as abusive tax avoidance, the GAAR under Article 19 of the Tax Administration Law empowers the tax authority to disregard the transaction and impose the tax that would have been paid had the substance been real.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly establish or maintain a shell-like structure and cause the Vietnamese LLC to sign non-arm's length contracts with related entities may be jointly responsible for the assessed tax shortages to the extent the legal entity is dissolved or unable to pay. Under the Enterprise Law 2020 and the Civil Code, the director who illegally transfers corporate assets or uses the corporate shell to evade tax obligations can be personally ordered to restore the company's assets or compensate the company. Immigration control: a legal representative with an outstanding tax assessment is prohibited from exiting Vietnam, and forward travel suspensions may be applied to shareholders who are also directors. Criminal liability arises under Article 213 of the Penal Code for releasing from settlement obligations or deliberately performing contrary to law in tax collection ("for-profit crimes") only if an official colludes; for the corporate director, the more likely exposure is Article 200 tax evasion and Article 196 of the Penal Code (intentionally violating state economic management regulations causing serious consequences).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Cross-Border Payment Route Offenses (AML)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the webnovel platform to launder illicit proceeds through in-app coin purchases, conducting transactions with criminal-derived funds, deliberate under-recording of Apple IAP/Google Play revenues to transfer funds to offshore accounts, using overseas shell payment processors, issuing payments without proper invoices, or acceptance of cryptocurrency payments as a deliberate act to avoid traceability and reporting obligations under the Law on Anti-Money Laundering (Law No. 14/2022/QH15, effective 1 March 2023) and Decree 116/2013/ND-CP amending Decree 19/2023. Non-reporting of large cross-border payment schemes through personal accounts is also treated as a serious red flag by the State Bank of Vietnam and the Government Inspectorate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the AML regime: reporting entities that fail to identify customers or report suspicious transactions face fines up to VND 200,000,000; failure to comply with internal control rules attracts fines up to VND 500,000,000; non-cooperation in a transaction freeze may result in additional fines. Foreign exchange violations under Ordinance on Foreign Exchange and Decree 88/2019/ND-CP can result in fines from VND 100,000,000 to VND 300,000,000, plus forced repatriation of funds. Where laundering of criminal proceeds is proven, criminal sanction under Article 324 of the Penal Code: imprisonment from 1 to 10 years for laundering money, with aggravating factors up to 15 years. The corporate entity can be subject to penal fines and dissolution/prohibition.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit the payment rails to be used for laundering, or who help structure transactions to obscure more than VND 300,000,000 in a single or multiple linked operations, face criminal imprisonment under Article 324 as principals or accomplices. Directors are additionally exposed to asset seizure, exit bans, and personal confiscation orders. Vietnamese courts and the State Bank may order the director to pay restitution, are permitted to freeze bank accounts and personal property of the director, and can impose a travel ban to prevent flight. The termination of a director from the legal entity does not extinguish the personal criminal liability. For a foreign-owned LLC, the offshore ultimate beneficial owner may be denied entry or extradition cooperation under treaty provisions; directors resident in Vietnam are the primary target of criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend Distribution and Repatriation Non-Compliance / Unlawful Capital Withdrawal
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to foreign shareholders before satisfying annual mandatory fund contributions under Vietnamese law, distributing dividends based on fictitious profits, withdrawing capital without lawful approval, failing to declare dividend income on the finalization return, or implementing an unauthorized deemed distribution through excessive related-party royalties or management fees instead of formal dividend payments to avoid the dividend CIT. Also failure of the LLC to withhold dividend CIT/VAT and to remit the withholding within the statutory deadline (within 30 days of distribution, relating to monthly/multi-period declaration rules) and failure to submit the withholding tax return to the local tax office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company is liable for the unpaid dividend withholding tax (10% CIT for corporate shareholders) and subject to late payment interest of 0.03% per day. Penalty for late or non-filing of withholding returns and non-payment of withheld taxes ranges up to VND 20,000,000 for each form and additional fines. Dividend distributions made in violation of the Enterprise Law 2020 (Article 135) render the shareholder liable to return any profits received from illegal distributions plus damages; the company's legal representative can be fined from VND 5,000,000 to VND 15,000,000 under the Enterprise Law administrative sanctions. If the profit repatriation is disguised as a royalty or interest payment to a foreign related party fabricated without substance, the entire amount is disallowed as a deduction and treated as a deemed dividend, triggering the additional 10% dividend CIT with penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and Directors who approve an unlawful dividend distribution can be jointly and severally liable to the company and to creditors for the value of the distributed amount and consequential losses under Article 135, Section 4, and Article 136 of the Enterprise Law 2020; the Civil Code allows affected creditors to pursue claims directly against the director. Travel bans and asset freezes apply for unsatisfied tax liabilities related to the distribution; directors can also face criminal prosecution under Article 200 of the Penal Code if the distribution goes hand in hand with tax under-declaration or the failure to remit withholding taxes constitutes misappropriation of state money (Article 221 - appropriating state revenues in the form of non-remitted withholding tax, potentially imprisonment for up to 10 years).
